Health & Status API

GET /api/v1/health

Description: Health check endpoint to verify API server is running.

Request

No parameters required.

curl http://localhost:9000/api/v1/health

Response

Success: 200 OK

{
  "status": "healthy"
}

Example (JavaScript)

fetch('/api/v1/health')
  .then(res => res.json())
  .then(data => console.log(data));

Virtual Hosts API

Manage virtual host configurations for intercepting and forwarding HTTP/HTTPS traffic.

GET /api/v1/vhosts

Description: List all configured virtual hosts.

Request

No parameters required.

curl http://localhost:9000/api/v1/vhosts

Response

Success: 200 OK

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "hostname": "api.example.com",
    "target_url": "https://real-backend.example.com",
    "enabled": true,
    "created_at": "2026-06-17T10:30:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-17T10:30:00Z"
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "hostname": "api.github.com",
    "target_url": "https://api.github.com",
    "enabled": true,
    "created_at": "2026-06-17T11:15:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-17T11:15:00Z"
  }
]

Response Fields

Field Type Description
id integer Unique identifier for the virtual host
hostname string The hostname to intercept (e.g., "api.example.com")
target_url string The backend URL to forward requests to
enabled boolean Whether this virtual host is active
created_at string ISO 8601 timestamp of creation
updated_at string ISO 8601 timestamp of last update
GET /api/v1/vhosts/{id}

Description: Get details of a specific virtual host.

Path Parameters

Parameter Type Required Description
id integer Required Virtual host ID

Request

curl http://localhost:9000/api/v1/vhosts/1

Response

Success: 200 OK

{
  "id": 1,
  "hostname": "api.example.com",
  "target_url": "https://real-backend.example.com",
  "enabled": true,
  "created_at": "2026-06-17T10:30:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-06-17T10:30:00Z"
}

Error: 400 Bad Request (Invalid ID)

{"error": "Invalid ID"}

Error: 404 Not Found (Virtual host not found)

{"error": "Virtual host not found"}
POST /api/v1/vhosts

Description: Create a new virtual host configuration.

Request Body

Field Type Required Description
hostname string Required Hostname to intercept (e.g., "api.example.com")
target_url string Required Backend URL to forward to (e.g., "https://backend.example.com")

Request

curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/api/v1/vhosts \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "hostname": "api.example.com",
    "target_url": "https://real-backend.example.com"
  }'

Response

Success: 201 Created

{
  "id": 3,
  "hostname": "api.example.com",
  "target_url": "https://real-backend.example.com",
  "enabled": true,
  "created_at": "2026-06-17T12:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-06-17T12:00:00Z"
}

Error: 400 Bad Request (Missing fields)

{"error": "Hostname and target_url are required"}

Error: 500 Internal Server Error

{"error": "Failed to create virtual host"}

Example (JavaScript)

fetch('/api/v1/vhosts', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    hostname: 'api.example.com',
    target_url: 'https://real-backend.example.com'
  })
})
  .then(res => res.json())
  .then(data => console.log('Created:', data));

  "created_at": "2026-06-17T10:30:00Z",

fetch('/api/v1/vhosts/1', {

DELETE /api/v1/vhosts/{id}

Description: Delete a virtual host configuration.

Path Parameters

Parameter Type Required Description
id integer Required Virtual host ID

Request

curl -X DELETE http://localhost:9000/api/v1/vhosts/1

Response

Success: 204 No Content

Error: 404 Not Found

    }
  });

HAR Export

GET /api/v1/vhosts/{id}/har

Description: Export all captured request/response logs for a virtual host as an HAR 1.2 (HTTP Archive) file. The resulting file can be imported into Chrome DevTools, Firefox Developer Tools, Charles Proxy, or any HAR-compatible analysis tool.

Path Parameters

Parameter Type Required Description
id integer Required Virtual host ID

Request

curl -o api.example.com.har http://localhost:9000/api/v1/vhosts/1/har

Response

Success: 200 OK

Returns a JSON file with Content-Disposition: attachment header. The filename is derived from the virtual host hostname (e.g., api.example.com.har).

{
  "log": {
    "version": "1.2",
    "creator": {
      "name": "spectre-proxy",
      "version": "1.0.0"
    },
    "entries": [
      {
        "startedDateTime": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
        "time": 125,
        "request": {
          "method": "GET",
          "url": "https://api.example.com/users",
          "httpVersion": "HTTP/1.1",
          "cookies": [],
          "headers": [
            {"name": "Accept", "value": "application/json"},
            {"name": "Host", "value": "api.example.com"}
          ],
          "queryString": [],
          "headersSize": -1,
          "bodySize": 0
        },
        "response": {
          "status": 200,
          "statusText": "OK",
          "httpVersion": "HTTP/1.1",
          "cookies": [],
          "headers": [
            {"name": "Content-Type", "value": "application/json"}
          ],
          "content": {
            "size": 42,
            "mimeType": "application/json",
            "text": "{\"users\": []}"
          },
          "redirectURL": "",
          "headersSize": -1,
          "bodySize": 42
        },
        "cache": {},
        "timings": {
          "send": 0,
          "wait": 125,
          "receive": 0
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

Error: 404 Not Found

{"error": "Virtual host not found"}

Response Headers

Header Value Description
Content-Type application/json HAR files are JSON documents
Content-Disposition attachment; filename="<hostname>.har" Triggers file download in browsers

HAR Entry Fields

Field Source Notes
startedDateTime Request timestamp ISO 8601 format
time duration_ms Total elapsed time in milliseconds
request.headers request_headers Converted from stored JSON map to HAR name/value pairs
response.content response_body Binary content is base64-encoded with encoding: "base64"
timings duration_ms Full duration assigned to wait; detailed breakdown not available

Example (JavaScript)

fetch('/api/v1/vhosts/1/har')
  .then(res => {
    const disposition = res.headers.get('Content-Disposition');
    const filename = disposition.match(/filename="(.+)"/)[1];
    return res.blob().then(blob => ({ blob, filename }));
  })
  .then(({ blob, filename }) => {
    const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
    const a = document.createElement('a');
    a.href = url;
    a.download = filename;
    a.click();
    URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
  });

Certificates API

Manage TLS certificates generated by the proxy for HTTPS interception.

GET /api/v1/certificates

Description: List all generated TLS certificates.

Request

curl http://localhost:9000/api/v1/certificates

Response

Success: 200 OK

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "hostname": "api.example.com",
    "created_at": "2026-06-17 10:30:00",
    "expires_at": "2027-06-17 10:30:00"
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "hostname": "api.github.com",
    "created_at": "2026-06-17 11:15:00",
    "expires_at": "2027-06-17 11:15:00"
  }
]

Response Fields

Field Type Description
id integer Unique identifier for the certificate
hostname string The hostname this certificate is for
created_at string Creation timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)
expires_at string Expiration timestamp (typically 1 year after creation)
GET /api/v1/certificates/ca

Description: Download the root CA certificate for installation on client systems.

Request

curl http://localhost:9000/api/v1/certificates/ca -o spectre-ca.crt

Response

Success: 200 OK

Content-Type: application/x-pem-file

Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=spectre-ca.crt

-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIDXTCCAkWgAwIBAgIUK...
(PEM-encoded certificate data)
...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----

Usage

After downloading, install the CA certificate on your system:

macOS:

sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot \
  -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain spectre-ca.crt

Linux:

sudo cp spectre-ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/
sudo update-ca-certificates

Windows:

certutil -addstore -f "ROOT" spectre-ca.crt
POST /api/v1/certificates/ca/replace

Description: Replace the root CA certificate with a custom one. All existing virtual host certificates will be invalidated and regenerated on-demand.

Request Body

Field Type Required Default Description
common_name string Required - Common Name (CN) for the CA certificate
organization string Optional "" Organization (O)
organizational_unit string Optional "" Organizational Unit (OU)
country string Optional "" Country (C)
province string Optional "" State/Province (ST)
locality string Optional "" Locality/City (L)
validity_years integer Optional 10 Certificate validity in years

Request

curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/api/v1/certificates/ca/replace \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "common_name": "My Company Root CA",
    "organization": "My Company Inc",
    "organizational_unit": "IT Security",
    "country": "US",
    "province": "New York",
    "locality": "New York City",
    "validity_years": 5
  }'

Minimal Request

Only the common_name is required:

curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/api/v1/certificates/ca/replace \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"common_name": "Custom CA"}'

Response

Success: 200 OK

{"message": "CA certificate replaced successfully"}

Error: 400 Bad Request (Missing common_name)

{"error": "common_name is required"}

Error: 500 Internal Server Error

{"error": "Failed to replace CA certificate"}

What Happens

  • ✅ New CA certificate is created with your custom fields
  • 🔄 Old CA is deactivated (preserved in database for audit)
  • 🗑️ All existing virtual host certificates are invalidated
  • ⚡ Certificate cache is cleared
  • 🔁 New certificates are automatically generated on-demand

Post-Replacement Steps

  1. Download the new CA certificate: GET /api/v1/certificates/ca
  2. Install the new CA in your system/browser trust store
  3. All subsequent HTTPS connections will use the new CA

Example (JavaScript)

fetch('/api/v1/certificates/ca/replace', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    common_name: 'My Custom CA',
    organization: 'My Organization',
    validity_years: 10
  })
})
  .then(res => res.json())
  .then(data => console.log(data.message));
POST /api/v1/certificates/ca/load

Description: Load a pre-generated CA certificate and private key. All existing virtual host certificates will be invalidated and regenerated on-demand.

Request Body

Field Type Required Description
certificate string Required PEM-encoded CA certificate
private_key string Required PEM-encoded CA private key

Request

curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/api/v1/certificates/ca/load \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIID...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
    "private_key": "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE...\n-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----"
  }'

Response

Success: 200 OK

{"message": "Custom CA certificate loaded successfully"}

Error: 400 Bad Request (Missing certificate)

{"error": "certificate is required"}

Error: 400 Bad Request (Missing private_key)

{"error": "private_key is required"}

Error: 500 Internal Server Error

{"error": "Failed to load CA certificate"}

What Happens

  • ✅ Custom CA certificate is loaded from provided PEM data
  • 🔄 Old CA is deactivated (preserved in database for audit)
  • 🗑️ All existing virtual host certificates are invalidated
  • ⚡ Certificate cache is cleared
  • 🔁 New certificates are automatically generated on-demand

Post-Load Steps

  1. Download the loaded CA certificate: GET /api/v1/certificates/ca
  2. Install the CA in your system/browser trust store
  3. All subsequent HTTPS connections will use the loaded CA

Example with File Upload (JavaScript)

// Read certificate and key files
const certFile = document.getElementById('certFile').files[0];
const keyFile = document.getElementById('keyFile').files[0];

const certificate = await certFile.text();
const private_key = await keyFile.text();

fetch('/api/v1/certificates/ca/load', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ certificate, private_key })
})
  .then(res => res.json())
  .then(data => console.log(data.message));

Request Logs API

Access captured HTTP/HTTPS request and response data.

GET /api/v1/logs

Description: List captured request logs with pagination.

Query Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Description
limit integer Optional 100 Number of logs to return (max per page)
offset integer Optional 0 Number of logs to skip (for pagination)

Request

curl "http://localhost:9000/api/v1/logs?limit=50&offset=0"

Response

Success: 200 OK

{
  "logs": [
    {
      "id": 123,
      "vhost_id": 1,
      "vhost_hostname": "api.example.com",
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/users/123",
      "query": "?format=json",
      "status_code": 200,
      "request_headers": "{\"User-Agent\":\"curl/7.81.0\",\"Accept\":\"*/*\"}",
      "response_headers": "{\"Content-Type\":\"application/json\"}",
      "request_body": "",
      "response_body": "{\"id\":123,\"name\":\"John Doe\"}",
      "timestamp": "2026-06-17T12:45:30Z",
      "duration_ms": 245
    },
    {
      "id": 122,
      "vhost_id": 2,
      "vhost_hostname": "api.github.com",
      "method": "POST",
      "path": "/repos/owner/repo/issues",
      "query": "",
      "status_code": 201,
      "request_headers": "{\"Authorization\":\"token ghp_xxx\"}",
      "response_headers": "{\"Content-Type\":\"application/json\"}",
      "request_body": "{\"title\":\"Bug report\"}",
      "response_body": "{\"id\":456,\"number\":1}",
      "timestamp": "2026-06-17T12:40:15Z",
      "duration_ms": 532
    }
  ],
  "total": 245,
  "limit": 50,
  "offset": 0
}

Response Fields

Field Type Description
logs array Array of request log objects
total integer Total number of logs in database
limit integer Limit used for this query
offset integer Offset used for this query

Log Object Fields

Field Type Description
id integer Unique identifier for the log entry
vhost_id integer ID of the virtual host that handled this request
vhost_hostname string Hostname of the virtual host
method string HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.)
path string Request path (e.g., "/users/123")
query string Query string (e.g., "?format=json")
status_code integer HTTP response status code
request_headers string JSON-encoded request headers
response_headers string JSON-encoded response headers
request_body string Request body content
response_body string Response body content
timestamp string ISO 8601 timestamp when request was captured
duration_ms integer Request duration in milliseconds

Pagination Example

# Get first 50 logs
curl "http://localhost:9000/api/v1/logs?limit=50&offset=0"

# Get next 50 logs
curl "http://localhost:9000/api/v1/logs?limit=50&offset=50"

# Get third page
curl "http://localhost:9000/api/v1/logs?limit=50&offset=100"
GET /api/v1/logs/{id}

Description: Get detailed information for a specific request log.

Path Parameters

Parameter Type Required Description
id integer Required Request log ID

Request

curl http://localhost:9000/api/v1/logs/123

Response

Success: 200 OK

{
  "id": 123,
  "vhost_id": 1,
  "vhost_hostname": "api.example.com",
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/users/123",
  "query": "?format=json",
  "status_code": 200,
  "request_headers": "{\"User-Agent\":\"curl/7.81.0\",\"Accept\":\"*/*\",\"Host\":\"api.example.com\"}",
  "response_headers": "{\"Content-Type\":\"application/json\",\"Content-Length\":\"42\"}",
  "request_body": "",
  "response_body": "{\"id\":123,\"name\":\"John Doe\",\"email\":\"john@example.com\"}",
  "timestamp": "2026-06-17T12:45:30Z",
  "duration_ms": 245
}

Error: 400 Bad Request (Invalid ID)

{"error": "Invalid ID"}

Error: 404 Not Found (Log not found)

{"error": "Request log not found"}

Example (JavaScript)

fetch('/api/v1/logs/123')
  .then(res => res.json())
  .then(log => {
    console.log(`${log.method} ${log.path}`);
    console.log('Request:', JSON.parse(log.request_headers));
    console.log('Response:', log.response_body);
  });

Quick Start Guide

Step 1: Download Root CA Certificate

curl http://localhost:9000/api/v1/certificates/ca -o spectre-ca.crt

Step 2: Install Root CA

macOS:

sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot \
  -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain spectre-ca.crt

Linux:

sudo cp spectre-ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/
sudo update-ca-certificates

Windows:

certutil -addstore -f "ROOT" spectre-ca.crt

Step 3: Add a Virtual Host

curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/api/v1/vhosts \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "hostname": "api.example.com",
    "target_url": "https://real-backend.example.com"
  }'

Step 4: Route Traffic to Proxy

echo "127.0.0.1 api.example.com" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts

Step 5: Test Interception

HTTP:

curl http://api.example.com:8080/endpoint

HTTPS:

curl https://api.example.com:8443/endpoint

Step 6: View Captured Traffic

curl http://localhost:9000/api/v1/logs | jq

Step 7: Export Traffic as HAR

Download the captured traffic for a virtual host as a HAR file, then open it in Chrome DevTools (Network tab → Import HAR) or any HAR viewer:

curl -o api.example.com.har http://localhost:9000/api/v1/vhosts/1/har
